title: Network Analyzer v2026
summary: A Linux terminal toolkit for authorized wireless discovery, passive monitoring, scan analysis, reporting, and explainable anomaly detection using locally learned baselines.
pageNote: This page combines the Network Analyzer v2026 overview, architecture, capabilities, authorized-use boundary, setup guide, validation workflow, and source links in one case study.

sections.label: Overview
sections.title: Authorized wireless visibility through a local, inspectable toolkit.
paragraphs: Network Analyzer is a Linux terminal application for authorized wireless discovery, local monitoring, saved-scan reporting, and investigation of unusual wireless behavior.

The Bash launcher prepares a project-local Python environment and transfers execution to a Python dispatcher. Scans, reports, logs, learned patterns, incidents, and optional local ML models remain on the operator's machine.

sections.label: Capabilities
sections.title: Discover, monitor, analyze, record, and investigate.
points: Perform passive wireless discovery and write CSV, normalized JSON, and local capture-log artifacts
Inspect access points, channels, signal observations, security indicators, and local risk summaries
Compare learned access-point patterns with trusted baselines and record explainable anomaly incidents
Import saved scans, replay observations, export incidents, and generate portable Markdown reports
Manage monitor-mode transitions and offer normal-network restoration after workflows finish
Present live views through tmux or optional graphical terminals that follow the terminal's actual size
Provide guided target discovery or manual entry for explicitly authorized active lab exercises
Maintain a passive, deduplicated access-point history through Dev Automate

sections.label: Architecture
sections.title: Python engine architecture behind a minimal Bash launcher.
paragraphs: network_analyzer.sh verifies Python, prepares .venv when required, and execs interactive.py. The Python dispatcher creates one shared NetworkAnalyzerCore instance and routes actions to focused engines.

Runtime information remains local. Discovery creates raw CSV and normalized JSON; analysis creates Markdown; anomaly learning persists snapshots, observations, patterns, trust decisions, and incidents in SQLite.

sections.label: Safety
sections.title: Wireless assessment requires an explicit authorization boundary.
paragraphs: Passive discovery, saved-data analysis, reporting, and anomaly review are the normal starting points. Operations that change adapter state or transmit management traffic can interrupt wireless service and belong only in an isolated lab or another expressly approved environment.
Scans, logs, reports, captures, SQLite databases, and trained models can contain SSIDs, BSSIDs, channels, signal observations, interface information, and other local telemetry.
sections.callout: Use Network Analyzer only against wireless environments and devices you own or are explicitly authorized to assess. Begin with passive workflows and validate active functionality in an isolated lab.

architecture.title: Local, engine-based terminal architecture
architecture.summary: A small Bash startup layer hands off to a Python dispatcher, specialized engines, local persistence, reporting, and optional terminal dashboards.
steps: network_analyzer.sh verifies Python, prepares .venv when required, and execs interactive.py.
interactive.py loads config.yaml, builds NetworkAnalyzerCore, and routes menu or CLI actions to an engine.
Core manages configuration, project-local interface state, readiness diagnostics, and privileged command preparation.
Discovery and monitor engines collect and parse local wireless observations into CSV, JSON, and capture-log artifacts.
Analysis and vulnerability modules summarize saved JSON and write Markdown reports.
AIAnomalyEngine stores snapshots and learned patterns in SQLite, creates explainable incidents, and trains a local Isolation Forest after the configured sample threshold.
Terminal and dashboard engines present live local views without creating a remote data service.

guide.title: Authorized operator quick guide
guide.summary: Install dependencies, confirm the approved assessment scope, run readiness diagnostics, select an adapter, and begin with passive discovery or saved-data analysis.
guide.audience: Linux users conducting authorized wireless assessments, lab exercises, or local network monitoring.
prerequisites: A supported Linux environment and, for live workflows, a compatible wireless adapter
Explicit authorization for the wireless environment
System tools required by the selected workflow, as reported by --doctor
steps: Review config.yaml and set output paths or thresholds if needed.
Run python3 interactive.py --doctor to review missing tools and packages.
Start ./network_analyzer.sh and select the intended wireless interface.
Use passive discovery or analyze existing JSON scans before any active workflow.
Export reports to reports/ and protect the generated local telemetry.
When finished, restore normal adapter mode if monitor mode was enabled.
verification: python3 -m compileall -q . completes without syntax errors.
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v passes without wireless hardware.
python3 interactive.py --doctor reports the current environment state.
A saved JSON scan can be summarized with menu option 10 and exported with option 11.
troubleshooting: If Python dependencies are unavailable, allow the launcher to create .venv or install python3-venv and rerun it.
If --doctor reports missing system commands, install only the packages required for the approved workflow and rerun the diagnostic.
If no adapter is listed, confirm the adapter is attached, unblocked, and supported by the Linux driver.
If connectivity does not return after monitor mode, use menu option 2 and then reconnect through the host network manager.
If anomaly output is noisy, collect more representative passive samples, review trusted baselines, and adjust thresholds in config.yaml.

validation.title: Offline regression and readiness validation
validation.summary: The included unit suite exercises parsing, report generation, monitor-state handling, dispatch, data persistence, and anomaly logic without requiring a wireless adapter or root. Live radio behavior must be tested only in an authorized lab.
